title: Tadla irrigated plain, Beni Moussa side, 14 Sep to 8 Oct 2026
summary: Between 14 Sep and 8 Oct 2026 the Tadla plain got brighter, with mean HH up 0.8 dB and 11.79 km2 brighter in HH inside the 9 km circle. The 8 Oct date carries a flag, so most of this brightening should not be read as change on the ground.

sections.heading: What changed
sections.text: Over 24 days mean HV moved by 0.34 dB and mean HH by 0.8 dB. In HV, 4.88 km2 turned brighter by more than 3 dB and 2.08 km2 darker; in HH, 11.79 km2 turned brighter and 3.44 km2 darker.

sections.heading: Where, by terrain type
sections.text: The brightening covers every type. Rough dry ground and fields had 5.38 km2 brighter in HH and rose 0.74 dB, and trees, shrub and rugged slopes rose 0.56 dB in HH. Built-up land, which should stay stable, rose 0.95 dB in HH. The changing fields had 1.64 km2 brighter and 1.08 km2 darker in HV.

sections.heading: Possible causes
sections.text: Possible cause: a processing offset in the 8 Oct product, since built-up land brightened like the fields; reprocessed files would settle it. Possible cause: a wet surface after rain, which raises the echo from soil and walls; rain records for October would check it. Possible cause for part of the field change: new crops; a field visit would check it.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: 8 Oct 2026 carries a flag: backscatter over built-up land shifted more than 0.5 dB from its June-September median, a possible processing offset or widespread wet conditions. It lowers confidence in every number from flagged dates. One track only, so field edges facing away from the radar can look darker.

sections.heading: What an agency could do next
sections.text: Use an unflagged date for any field figure, check rain records for October, and ask NASA whether the October products will be reprocessed.
